title: Message
description: Canonical wire envelope for a single SOX message. This is the authoritative schema for the stored and delivered message shape. See spec/protocol.md §Message envelope shape for normative field semantics. Implementations that inline this schema (e.g. recv.output.schema.json) MUST match this definition exactly.

channel.description: Name of the channel this message was sent to. Reserved prefixes: 'dm/<sorted-pair>' (server-enforced two-party), 'group/<group-id>' (server-enforced membership), 'sox/' (server-emitted derived channels, agents cannot write).

sender.description: agent_id of the agent that sent the message. Server-certified: bound from the verified connection identity, not self-reported by the client. In federated v2 deployments, takes the form '<server-id>/<agent-id>'; in v1.0 single-server deployments, a bare agent-id string.

body.description: Opaque message payload. MUST be a JSON object. SOX does not inspect or validate the body beyond requiring it to be an object. Recommended advisory fields: 'type' (string), 'subject' (string), 'context' (string), 'question' (string), 'answer' (string), 'urgency' (one of low/normal/high). Reserved body types with normative schemas: 'sox-error' (spec/envelopes/sox-error.schema.json), 'sox-invite' (spec/envelopes/sox-invite.schema.json).

correlation_id.description: Optional caller-supplied correlation token. Stored verbatim and echoed back in recv output. Use for: request-reply pairing, thread anchoring. The protocol does not enforce uniqueness. Null when not needed.

sent_at.description: Unix epoch seconds (floating-point) at which the backing store accepted the message. Retained for backward compatibility; seq is the authoritative ordering key within a channel.

message_id.description: Backing-store-assigned unique identifier for this message. Use as reply_to when replying, or as the reference in channels__ack calls.

seq.description: Per-channel monotone counter starting at 1. Authoritative ordering key within a channel. Used as the cursor for replay (since parameter). Assigned by the server; never set by the sender. See docs/decisions/seq-ordering-scope.md.

ts.description: Server-assigned monotonic nanosecond timestamp. Advisory tiebreaker for cross-channel display ordering. NOT globally total-ordered in multi-node or federated deployments. Null if the server does not support nanosecond timestamps. See docs/decisions/seq-ordering-scope.md.

reply_to.description: message_id of the parent message in a thread. Null if this message is not a reply. Set by the sender via send input. Used for thread expansion (thread_depth on recv) and wait-graph computation for deadlock detection. See docs/decisions/threading-depth.md.

delivered_to.description: Agent IDs that have recv'd this message. Populated by the server as agents drain their mailbox. Used for deadlock detection wait-graph computation at query time. Null if the server has not yet delivered this message to any agent, or if the server does not implement delivered_to tracking (SHOULD-implement feature). See docs/decisions/deadlock-detection-approach.md.

origin_server.description: Server ID in federated deployments. Always null in single-server v1.0 deployments. Reserved for federated v2 where agent identities take the form '<server-id>/<agent-id>'. See docs/decisions/federation-scope.md.

_meta.description: Optional observability metadata. Present when include_meta is true (default) on the recv call. Absent when include_meta is false. See docs/decisions/observability-meta-mode.md.

body.subject: Which database schema version should I target?
body.question: The task mentions schema v2 but the repo shows v3 in production. Which do I use?
